questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: ABCD is a rhombus (a parallelogram with all four sides congruent), with diagonals meeting at E. Prove that AC ⊥ BD.
questions.prompt_markup: ABCD is a rhombus (a parallelogram with all four sides congruent), with diagonals meeting at E. Prove that AC ⊥ BD.
questions.required_method: Use that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, then SSS on triangles AEB and AED (or the perpendicular bisector converse).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: BE = ED (diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other); AB = AD; AE = AE; △AEB ≅ △AED (SSS); ∠AEB ≅ ∠AED form a linear pair, so both are 90°. Alternative: A and C are each equidistant from B and D, so AC is the perpendicular bisector of BD.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A parallelogram has vertices A(0, 0), B(a, 0), C(a + b, c), D(b, c), with a > 0 and c > 0. Prove that AB = DC and AD = BC.
questions.prompt_markup: A parallelogram has vertices A(0, 0), B(a, 0), C(a + b, c), D(b, c), with a > 0 and c > 0. Prove that AB = DC and AD = BC.
questions.correct_answer: AB = DC = a and AD = BC = √(b² + c²)
questions.required_method: Use the distance formula on each pair of opposite sides.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: AB = a; DC = |a + b - b| = a; AD = √(b² + c²); BC = √((a + b - a)² + c²) = √(b² + c²).

questions.correct_answer: Any parallelogram can be moved (rigid motion) so that A is at the origin and AB lies on the positive x-axis; then D = (b, c) and C = B + (D - A) = (a + b, c).
